# Taught Selectors Over Guessed Labels

Stop trying to *infer* which UI element is which from its text, and let the user **point at it once**.
Store the stable identifier — a view ID — and match on that afterwards. Text guessing is a bet on
someone else's copywriting and locale; a taught selector is a fact the user supplied.

## The failure that produced it

[[farely]] first shipped `PAUSE_LABELS` / `RESUME_LABELS`: keyword lists meant to find a "pause" control
in Bolt, Uber and FreeNow. The premise itself was wrong, and the CHANGELOG says so plainly rather than
quietly deleting it:

> "Correcting a wrong premise: no ride app ships a \"Pause\" button, and the real controls
> (online/offline toggle, \"Stop new requests\", trip / ID-check markers) differ per app + locale and
> are often icons with no matchable text."
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/CHANGELOG.md, 2026-07-12

Three distinct defeats for label guessing in one sentence: the control may not exist, its name varies
per app and language, and it may be an **icon with no text at all**. No amount of keyword tuning
recovers from the third.

## The replacement — Learn-controls

The driver opens the target app, Farely watches, and the driver tags the real node. What gets stored is
a selector, matched **view-ID-first** with text as a weaker fallback — `flagReportViewIds` on the
accessibility service is what makes those IDs visible in the first place, see
[[android-accessibility-service]]. Coverage is displayed as a fraction (0/4 → 2/4 in the recorded
manual checks), so the user can see what the app still cannot do.

## Boundaries

Tagging is restricted to **chore controls** — the multi-app housekeeping actions. A ride offer's Accept
button can never become a taught selector; that exclusion is enforced separately and argued on
[[never-automate-the-accept-tap]]. A general-purpose "teach me any button" mechanism would have
dissolved the product's central safety rule, so the teaching surface is deliberately narrower than the
technique allows.

## Where else it applies

Any automation over an interface you do not own and cannot version-pin: browser extensions over third
party sites, RPA over enterprise apps, test suites over someone else's front end. The same trade
appears in [[farely]]'s reading path, where a structured node read beats an inferred one —
[[node-tree-read-before-ocr]] — and it is the same instinct as
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]: prefer the value that was *given* to the value that was
*derived*, and record which one you have.

## Cost

It is unusable on first launch. Every taught selector is an onboarding step, and the app must degrade
gracefully to zero coverage — which it does, by simply not offering chore automation until taught.
